extracted.intended_audience: public relations practitioners, corporate communicators, PR students and communication professionals (primarily Chennai/India)
extracted.subtask_description: Objectives and mission statements of the PRSI Chennai Chapter describing professional-development goals, ethical expectations, education and industry–institution linkages for PR practitioners. Applicable to organizational practice and standards for PR work in the region.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a forum for PR and communication professionals to meet, interact and enhance their professional skills
rubrics_metrics.description: To provide a forum for PR and communication professionals to meet, interact and enhance their professional skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This objective signals that the chapter evaluates/values activities that enable peer interaction, networking, and skill-building (e.g., monthly meetings, seminars, workshops). Emphasis is on opportunities that contribute to professional skill enhancement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep abreast of the changing socio-economic, political, cultural and media scene and the changing role of public relations and communication
rubrics_metrics.description: To keep abreast of the changing Socio-economic, political, cultural and media scene and the changing role of public relations and communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied criterion for good PR practice: work should reflect awareness of contemporary socio-economic, political, cultural and media contexts and adapt the role of PR accordingly. Activities or outputs that demonstrate contextual awareness are valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep abreast of emerging concepts and tools of public relations and communication
rubrics_metrics.description: To keep abreast of emerging concepts and tools of public relations and communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This emphasizes adoption and familiarity with new methods, technologies and approaches in PR—e.g., digital tools, measurement techniques, integrated communications—when evaluating practitioner competence or programme relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help promote ethical standards in public relations
rubrics_metrics.description: To help promote ethical standards in public relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear normative criterion: PR work (including press releases and campaigns) should conform to accepted ethical standards. Although the page does not enumerate specific ethics rules, promoting and upholding ethical practice is an explicit organizational objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote PR education
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valuation of educational activities: training programmes, apprenticeships, linkages with academic bodies and promotion of PR as a subject of management studies are considered important measures of professional contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and award excellence in public relations and communication
rubrics_metrics.description: To recognize and award Excellence in Public Relations and communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chapter intends to identify and honor outstanding PR work. While specific award criteria are not listed on this page, 'excellence' is an explicit objective and thus a standard the organization seeks to apply through recognition programmes.

rubrics_metrics.name: 360° communications coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chapter has an ongoing tradition of successfully organising seminars, workshops, site visits and training programmes besides monthly meetings, collectively covering 360° communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied quality dimension: communications activities and practitioner skillsets should be comprehensive and integrated across channels and functions (a '360°' perspective). Programs or outputs demonstrating multi-channel, holistic communications are aligned with the chapter's goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry–institution linkages and apprenticeships
rubrics_metrics.description: It has a strong industry-institution association and Communication students benefit immensely out of apprenticeships and the opportunity to learn from the practitioners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion for educational/practice quality: strong ties between industry and academic institutions and provision of apprenticeships or practitioner-led learning experiences are considered measures of effectiveness for PR education and professional development.
